trends.name: AI agents bypassing access controls and creating credential exposure risks
trends.rationale: Multiple sources confirm that AI agents are creating systemic credential and access control gaps. The 2026 State of Agent Security Report identifies ~1,280 third-party AI products with 282 behind SSO and ~1,000 invisible to identity infrastructure (Oct 10). Apple is tightening macOS Full Disk Access controls specifically due to AI agent security risks (Oct 5). SailPoint's Horizons of Identity Security report highlights a 'velocity paradox' where security architectures lag AI deployment (Oct 9). GitGuardian reports the credential layer is expanding faster than security teams can see it (Oct 5).

trends.name: Third-party software supply chain vulnerabilities enabling high-impact breaches
trends.rationale: Multiple high-impact breaches demonstrate third-party dependencies as primary attack vectors. Bitget lost $388M via an unpatched flaw in a third-party security product (Sept 28), credential-stealing GitHub Actions workflows were planted in 340+ repositories via compromised maintainer accounts (Oct 9), FortiBleed harvested 86,644 Fortinet device credentials from internet-facing appliances (Oct 7), and the tensorlake npm package was compromised to deliver credential-stealing malware (Oct 8). ASOS breach demonstrates single compromised identity leading to deep network penetration (Oct 9).

trends.name: Phishing campaigns targeting AI product platforms and credentials at scale
trends.rationale: Multiple coordinated phishing campaigns target AI platform adoption and decision-makers. A human-operated phishing platform impersonates advertising products for ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Perplexity, and other AI chatbots to capture credentials and MFA codes (Oct 6). China-nexus TA419 executed credential phishing campaigns specifically targeting AI experts at U.S. think tanks, universities, and legal organizations (Oct 4). Wazza phishing kit demonstrates evolved infrastructure with filtering, session management, and traffic controls targeting banking, government, and manufacturing (Oct 8).

trends.name: Security integrator market consolidation and professionalization accelerating
trends.rationale: Multiple signals show accelerating market consolidation and standardization. ESA launched its Industry Performance Index to help integrators benchmark performance (Sept 28), GSX 2026 achieved record attendance of 16,000+ registrants from 100 countries with 17% growth over 2025 (Sept 28). Securitas Technology acquired Sonitrol El Paso (Oct 1) and Pye-Barker acquired Union AlarmTronic (Sept 30), continuing consolidation trend. ADI is investing heavily in integrator-enabling design and professional services (Oct 8).

trends.name: AI overlay solutions for legacy camera systems enabling cost-effective modernization
trends.rationale: Industry sources confirm AI-as-overlay becomes the next deployment wave rather than forklift replacement. Security Sales reports that the next wave of security AI will layer onto existing camera infrastructure, fundamentally changing integrator business models (Oct 2). Securitas Technology's 2027 Global Technology Outlook Report highlights how AI and connected security ecosystems are reshaping security through backward-compatible deployment (Oct 5). This creates new service opportunities for integrators without requiring customers to replace operational systems.

articles.title: How to Add Security AI to the Camera Already on the Wall
Securitas Technology Releases 2027 Global Technology Outlook Report

trends.name: Video evidence integrity and authentication gaining industry focus
trends.rationale: SWEAR launched the Community Video Integrity Project designed to add an independent, complementary layer of video authentication and chain-of-custody verification (Oct 1). This demonstrates emerging industry recognition that video evidence authentication is becoming a critical operational requirement for physical security deployments, particularly in contexts where video evidence must withstand legal or forensic scrutiny.

articles.title: SWEAR Launches Video Evidence Integrity Protection Program

trends.name: Agentic threat actors conducting destructive cloud infrastructure attacks
trends.rationale: JadePuffer, characterized as an AI-powered threat actor, compromised an Azure tenant and conducted destructive attacks deleting cloud-based storage, applications, and databases, reportedly using exposed credentials (Sept 28). This represents the emergence of autonomous adversaries leveraging AI capabilities to conduct large-scale destructive attacks against cloud infrastructure, distinct from traditional credential theft.

articles.title: JadePuffer AI Actor Compromises Azure Tenant in Destructive Cloud Attack

trends.name: Multifamily residential property access control transitioning from mechanical to digital systems
trends.rationale: Security Sales reports that multifamily security is moving beyond traditional mechanical keys toward digital access control systems where property managers know who has access to what and why (Oct 9). This represents a shift in how integrators approach residential property security, moving from perimeter-focused mechanical solutions to identity-and-access-focused digital systems, creating new market opportunities for access control integrators.

articles.title: How Integrators Move Multifamily Security Beyond Traditional Keys

trends.name: False alarm financial liability becoming quantified industry metric
trends.rationale: Interface Systems released a study revealing that false alarm liabilities comprise 80% of the financial burden for multi-location businesses (Oct 9). This quantification of false alarm costs as a primary financial metric suggests the industry is moving toward treating alarm false positives as a measurable operational and financial risk factor rather than an accepted business cost.

articles.title: Interface Systems Report Exposes Hidden Cost of False Alarms

trends.name: China-aligned threat actors targeting US AI policy expertise and decision-makers
trends.rationale: China-nexus cyber espionage group TA419 executed multiple credential phishing campaigns targeting AI experts at U.S. think tanks, universities, and legal sector organizations (Oct 4). This represents strategic targeting of American AI policy influencers and technical expertise holders by state-aligned actors using AitM phishing techniques, indicating AI policy infrastructure has become a high-priority espionage target.

articles.title: China-Aligned TA419 Targets U.S. AI Policy Experts With Microsoft AitM Phishing

trends.name: Credential harvesting from internet-facing appliances remains active threat
trends.rationale: FBI and Secret Service warned that the FortiBleed credential harvesting campaign targeting internet-facing Fortinet FortiGate firewalls and SSL VPN gateways remains active and has amassed 86,644 device credentials (Oct 7). This demonstrates that large-scale, persistent credential harvesting against perimeter security appliances continues to be a viable attack vector despite public awareness.

articles.title: FBI Warns FortiBleed Remains Active After Amassing 86,644 Fortinet Device Credentials

trends.name: Malware abusing privileged drivers to disable security monitoring
trends.rationale: Lunex Stealer malware distributed via compromised Ukrainian websites abuses AMD drivers to disable security monitoring and steal browser credentials as part of a wider malware-as-a-service platform (Sept 26). This demonstrates sophisticated attack chains that use legitimate driver vulnerabilities to bypass endpoint security controls and enable credential theft at scale.

articles.title: Lunex Stealer Abuses AMD Driver to Disable Security Monitoring and Steal Browser Credentials

trends.name: Sophisticated phishing kits adding session management and traffic control capabilities
trends.rationale: Security researchers identified Wazza, a phishing kit that goes beyond copying login pages to include filtering, session management, and traffic controls in the infrastructure delivering phishing pages (Oct 8). This represents an evolution in phishing infrastructure sophistication, where attackers are building enterprise-grade capabilities into their attack delivery mechanisms.

articles.title: Wazza Phishkit Targets Banking, Government, and Manufacturing Across the US, EU, and Australia

trends.name: AI-powered visual analytics platforms consolidating multiple security functions
trends.rationale: Securitas Technology and IQSIGHT won a best electronic security project award for a platform combining visual analytics, alarm management, and live communication (Sept 24). Securitas Technology also released a 2027 Global Technology Outlook Report highlighting how AI, cloud platforms and connected security ecosystems are reshaping security (Oct 5).

trends.name: Malware exploiting legitimate security tools and driver infrastructure to evade detection
trends.rationale: Two separate malware campaigns across 14 days demonstrate attackers weaponizing legitimate software and kernel-level infrastructure meant to protect systems. Lunex stealer malware abuses AMD drivers to disable security monitoring while stealing browser credentials (Sept 26). CLOSEDQUORUM malware uses AI model voting to dynamically select theft targets while evading traditional detection (Sept 23). Both incidents show attackers bypassing security infrastructure at the driver level rather than defeating detection through obfuscation alone.

trends.name: OSDP training and standards adoption reaching market inflection point
trends.rationale: SIA and AMAG Technology launched a new tiered OSDP training program (Sept 24) aimed at equipping sales and marketing professionals with foundational knowledge. This signals industry recognition that OSDP adoption requires education beyond technical implementation, suggesting OSDP standardization is becoming a competitive differentiator in access control systems.

articles.title: SIA, AMAG Technology Launching New OSDP Training Program

trends.rationale: SWEAR launched the Community Video Integrity Project (Oct 1) designed to add an independent, complementary layer of video authentication and evidence integrity protection. This signals emerging industry recognition that video evidence authentication and chain-of-custody verification are becoming critical for physical security deployments.

articles.title: SWEAR Launches Video Evidence Integrity Protection Program

trends.name: AI overlay solutions for legacy camera systems enabling cost-effective modernization
trends.rationale: Security Sales reports that the next wave of AI adoption will layer onto existing camera infrastructure rather than requiring complete system replacement, fundamentally changing integrator business models (Oct 2). This represents a significant shift toward backward-compatible AI deployment that reduces customer capital requirements and creates new service opportunities for integrators.

articles.title: How to Add Security AI to the Camera Already on the Wall

trends.name: Access control modernization in government and hospitality sectors
trends.rationale: Two major sector-specific access control modernization initiatives were announced within days. The U.S. Marine Corps modernized barracks access management with LenelS2 (Sept 18), supporting the Barracks 2030 modernization effort with centralized management and enhanced security. Keenfinity Group created MiCOS as a focused access control solutions business (Sept 18), signaling renewed market demand for specialized access control. Both initiatives target high-security or regulated environments seeking to blend physical access control with operational efficiency.
